task: TASK 1 (tool and negatives), TASK 2 (entry and patch), TASK 3 (calibration) and TASK 4 (gap alignment, rejection pool, budget)
case_notes: The control case is SPEC-009's probe build: bedroom full_02's own floor_plan, seed 37 and height/thickness/door/window/skirting overrides with only compose_indoors.populate_assets_enabled flipped to True. It is the room the 0.1265 m2 intrusion was measured on, so it is the对照 that makes 'the constraint changed something' a measurement.

'gap_categories' is the fixture's own declaration (ADR-009 decision 11): the categories this room's retrieval vocabulary cannot cover, which is the only set generation is allowed to produce. A declared category the retrieval vocabulary *does* cover is BACKGROUND_NOT_A_GAP, because a matrix that declared itself work to do would pass without generation doing anything.
'min_generated_categories' is the lower bound the fixture keeps on the case (ADR-009 decision 11) so the matrix cannot pass by having no gaps at all.

'expect_failures' are prefixes the case must show in TASK 1. They come from the recorded evidence (SPEC-009 probe: 0.1265 m2 protected, 0.0315 m2 corridor; upstream default abort_unsatisfied=False; nothing about this build's patch or pin was recorded), not from the tool's output.
The kitchen and office cases have no probe build yet. They are listed with the delivery that defines their room and are reported not_run with that reason rather than passed.

The injected case shares the control's room, so the two rows are the same bedroom before and after the constraint: the control is SPEC-009's probe (0.1265 m2 protected, 0.0315 m2 corridor), and the injected row is SPEC-011 TASK 2's own build of it.

TASK 4: 'gap_categories' is now carried into the build as well as declared here -- the request in reservations.json lists the same categories, the pool refuses anything outside them, and the audit refuses a case whose two declarations disagree (BACKGROUND_CONSTRAINT_INPUT_MISMATCH(...:gaps)). A declaration that only the audit can see would be a rule the build was never given.

TASK 4: the per-stage allowance is GENERATED_OBJECTS_MAX_PER_STAGE (contract constant, 24), and a case's own 'budget' key now *overrides* it rather than being the only source. The frozen number is why three cases stopped declaring BACKGROUND_BUDGET_EXCEEDED; the control's 32 still shows it, and that is the case the cap exists for.

cases.note: TASK 4 changed two of this case's declarations, and both changes are consequences of the calibration rather than of the tool: (1) BACKGROUND_BUDGET_EXCEEDED(populate_assets) is gone because the allowance is now the frozen constant GENERATED_OBJECTS_MAX_PER_STAGE=24 and this room generated 13 -- the cap that must catch the un-injected control's 32 (which still shows it) is deliberately above the largest measured injected room (19, kitchen); (2) BACKGROUND_POOL_UNRECORDED is declared new: this build ran generation before the pool existed, so its objects were never judged. It stays red on requirement 4 (the room has covered categories in it) and on requirement 5 (abort off), and it is the case the pooled build (bedroom_pooled_37) is the red-to-green pair for.

cases.case_note: The build is the opt-in probe at the first weights (60/25), abort off: 19 generated objects and 0.0000 m2 in all three regions. Its no-injection control cannot be built in this environment (the wrapper run died on the missing `extra_mesh_objects` Blender extension, which NatureShelfTrinketsFactory's rock variants require and which fires by draw, not by room type). The seed here was declared 20 while the case never ran; the room's own seed is 23 (delivery and build command agree), so the declaration is corrected rather than left as a claim.
cases.note: TASK 4 revised two declarations here and both are recorded rather than dropped: (1) the allowance is the frozen constant (19 generated <= 24), so BACKGROUND_BUDGET_EXCEEDED is gone -- it is the control's 32 that the cap exists to catch; (2) BACKGROUND_GAP_UNFILLED(mirror_frame) is gone because that gap now carries a named reason: this build recorded no pool, so all that can be measured is that no object of the category is in the room (not-in-the-room(...), GAP_UNFILLED_KINDS[2]) -- which is an accounting, and the failure is reserved for a gap with no reason at all. The build itself is the same 19-object, 0.0000 m2 room TASK 3 measured; nothing about it was re-run or edited.

cases.case_note: The office could not be built at the first weights (60/25): that run died on the same missing extension. It built at the sweep's protecting setting (6/2.5), 18 generated objects, and **the protected region is still intruded by 0.0400 m2** (KitchenCabinetFactory 0.0245 + SingleCabinetFactory 0.0155) -- recorded as "the constraint was sent and it still intrudes", which is the outcome TASK 3 says must not be smoothed over.
cases.note: TASK 3 recorded this room honestly as 'the constraint was sent and it still intrudes': 18 generated objects, two cabinets 0.0400 m2 inside the protected region. TASK 4 mapped the three factories it exposed (KitchenCabinetFactory and SingleCabinetFactory to `cabinet`, PlantContainerFactory to `plant` -- all three covered by retrieval, so generating them is not filling a gap), which replaces the BACKGROUND_FACTORY_UNMAPPED declaration with the BACKGROUND_NOT_A_GAP one: the same five objects, judged instead of unjudged. It keeps its two overlap declarations and gains the solve_small abort (upstream's own obj_ontop_obj/desk groups). The allowance declaration is gone for the same reason as the kitchen's.

cases.case_note: TASK 4's answer to office_medium_20, same room and same weights (6/2.5) with the rejection pool on: 18 realised objects, 11 refused by name (2 of them for standing 0.0245/0.0155 m2 inside the protected region -- the un-pooled run's own two numbers -- and all 11 for not being a gap), 7 kept, and the ruler measures 0.0000 m2 in every region. It is red on requirement 5 alone, and that red is upstream's own constraint groups (lighting, desk, office_desk_chairs), not ours: turning abort_unsatisfied on in these rooms kills the build in ~20 s (TASK 3, measured). Requirement 4's two unfilled gaps (book_column, shelf) are accounted for by name: the pool judged every object and the sampler proposed neither category.

The control room at the first weights (60/25) with the rejection pool on: 13 realised objects became 5 (the three gap categories this run proposed), 8 refused by name (a monitor for not being declared here, the rest for being covered by retrieval), 0.0000 m2 in all three regions, 198.3 s. Red on requirement 5 alone, and those unsatisfied groups are upstream's own (lighting, desk, office_desk_chairs) -- `BACKGROUND_RESERVATION_UNSATISFIED` would name ours, and it does not fire. The two unfilled gaps (book_stack, mirror_frame) are accounted for: the pool judged every realised object, and neither category was proposed.

The kitchen at the first weights (60/25) with the pool on: 19 realised objects became 10, 9 refused by name, 0.0000 m2 in all three regions, 112.5 s. One refusal is a book column refused as not-declared-in-this-case -- book_column is a gap-eligible category the kitchen never asked for, which is the distinction the two not-a-gap sub-reasons exist to make. Red on requirement 5 alone, and those groups are upstream's own.

TASK 5's delivery: the pipeline's own run (office_pick_cup, variant seed 20, --no-replan, Isaac on) with SPEC-011's opt-in on. 7 kept / 11 refused, 0.0000 m2 in all three regions measured on the delivery's own build, and the room is the same one the generation-off run built (the two builds' shell measurements are identical key for key). Red on requirement 5 alone, and those groups are upstream's own -- BACKGROUND_RESERVATION_UNSATISFIED never fires. The delivery's manifest carries the same ledger under `background`.

negatives.name: no_separation_intrusion_returns
negatives.note: The control build's own measured intrusion (0.1265 m2 protected, 0.0315 m2 corridor) with the injection removed. The numbers are the probe's, not invented.

negatives.name: abort_switch_off
negatives.note: A run that solved everything with the switch off is still the run whose next build is silent.

negatives.name: unsatisfied_solve_continued
negatives.note: The probe's own log: 3 unsatisfied groups in solve_medium ('lighting', 'desk', 'office_desk_chairs') and the build carried on.

negatives.name: covered_category_generated
negatives.note: A generated desk: retrieval covers desk.n.01, so generating one is not filling a gap.

negatives.name: gap_declared_but_covered
negatives.note: The other direction of the same rule: the fixture declaring a covered category as a gap.

negatives.name: rejections_unbounded
negatives.note: The same candidate attempted 3 times (ATTEMPTS_PER_CANDIDATE_MAX is 2).

negatives.name: reservation_object_leaked
negatives.note: ADR-009 Consequences: the reservation object is invisible geometry, so this negative belongs to requirement 9 even though it is not one of the six.

negatives.name: factory_unmapped
negatives.note: An upstream factory the table does not name cannot be judged either way, so it is reported rather than allowed.

negatives.name: gap_unfilled_unaccounted
negatives.note: Requirement 4's second half: a declared gap with nothing generated for it and no named reason is a failure, not silence.

negatives.name: pool_not_recorded
negatives.note: Generation happened and the room has no rejection pool: the objects stood in the room unjudged, which is the probe build's own state (its 0.1265 m2 shelf is the result). ADR-009 decision 8: the pool is the fallback that must run whatever the constraints do.

negatives.name: pool_ledger_incomplete
negatives.note: The realistic shape of this bug: the ledger says the piece was refused (a rejection row names it) and the ruler measures it still standing in the protected region and in the corridor -- a deletion that did not happen. The intruder is in the ledger on purpose: an intruder the ledger never mentions is the overlap failure's own business.

negatives.name: reservation_term_unsatisfied
negatives.note: Upstream's unsatisfied-constraint report is keyed by the constraint's own name (evaluator/evaluate.py:262-275), so a name carrying our prefix is our term failing. TASK 3 attributed every unsatisfied group in every build to upstream's own lighting/desk/office_desk_chairs; this negative is what keeps that an attribution rather than a hope.
